newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Van Miert hopes for deal on BA-American plan.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert hopes for deal on BA-American plan.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Friday he hoped a satisfactory settlement could be found for the competition problems posed by the alliance between British Airways and AMR's American Airlines.
But he stressed that if Britain cleared the deal without giving due attention to the Comission's concerns, he would take the case to the European Court of Justice.

"I do sincerely hope that it will still be possible, in the spirit of full cooperation between the Commission and the member states...to find a fully adequate reply to all the competition concerns expressed by the Commission," he said in a statement.

The statement follows British Prime Minister John Major's comments in the House of Commons on Thursday that the Commission's views would be considered, "but it will be for the (President of Britain's Board of Trade) to decide whether to clear the alliance".

Major's comments were widely seen in the British press as further proof that the British government will jealously guard its competence to assess the transatlantic alliance despite Van Miert's threats.

Last Friday, in a letter to the Department of Trade and Industry distributed to the press in Brussels, the EU Commissioner appeared to be on a collision course with Britain over the controversial airline link-up.

The deal is currently being vetted both by the Commission and Britain's competition authority, the Office of Fair Trading (OFT). Earlier this month the two airlines also submitted it for clearance to the U.S. Department of Transportation.
While the Commission does not question Britain's right to examine the case, it has made crystal clear that the British decision could not conflict with the EU's assessment.

But the OFT's preliminary ruling on the alliance does precisely that. Early in December, it anounced it would clear the deal conditional on the two airlines agreeing to give up 168 weekly landing amd takeoff slots at congested London Heathrow airport.
BA indicated it would surrender the slots if it could sell them -- something Van Miert and EU Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock have said is not legal under European civil aviation rules.

Van Miert's statement stressed that the EU was investigating several other transatlantic alliances which also involved powerful European airlines and governments -- but none appeared to have challenged the Commission's authority so openly.

"I would like to recall, in this context, that in its ongoing analysis of the Lufthansa /United Airlines alliance, the German authorities involved fully cooperate with my Department", the statement said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
